correctness.rationale: For r≤d the first r translate moments form an invertible Vandermonde system, so any nontrivial integer combination has a nonconstant coefficient that is a nonzero rational multiple of α. Its leading nonzero nonconstant term stays irrational on any arithmetic progression after dividing by a fixed modulus. Weyl and the floor-residue boxes therefore give joint uniform residues with n and the claimed lcm denominator. Inclusion–exclusion gives the displayed local factors; for two equal exponents a single increment increases the exponent by 2 and both by 3, while for unequal exponents the two separate increments cost 1 and 2. For tightness, the full-N large-prime estimate quoted from Holdridge is exactly what is needed. The exact statement of Theorem 1.3 was inaccessible, but the required tail can also be derived from the natural-density coprimality result announced in Holdridge’s PDF abstract (its one-polynomial case, with Weyl equidistribution assured by an irrational leading coefficient). In detail, write n=am with a the part supported on primes ≤R. A common prime >R then gives gcd(m,⌊f(am)⌋)>1, while no prime ≤R divides both. For each fixed a this latter superset has density c_R=∏_{p≤R}(1−p⁻²)−1/ζ(2), by fixed-prime Weyl and the one-polynomial coprimality theorem applied to f(a·), which still has irrational leading coefficient. Summing the limsup bound c_R/a over smooth a is justified by the summable majorant 1/a for fixed R. The resulting bound c_R ∏_{p≤R}(1−1/p)⁻¹ is O(R⁻¹/²): c_R=O(1/R) and bounding the reciprocals of odd primes by those of odd integers gives O(√R) for the inverse product. This checks the needed large-prime step without relying on the exact wording of Theorem 1.3. A finite union over shifts and the fixed-p bound p⁻²ᴷ control all tails. CRT gives the same finite-prime laws as the shared Haar model, whose gcd ideals almost surely have finite positive generators since ∑_p r/p² converges. Every specified finite valuation profile has positive probability, and at all other primes the factors are 1−O_r(p⁻²). For d+1 consecutive shifts the integer finite difference of the floor values lies within 2^d of αd!; the choice α>2^d/d! irrational and p>αd!+2^d excludes all simultaneous multiples despite the positive proposed formula. This is existential in α for each d, not failure for every α. The uploaded finite checker was inspected, not executed and not used for the limit.

value.rationale: Gives a complete law and exact local correlations for the natural shared-coordinate problem, not just the frequency of one common gcd being 1.
